question: At a 55-mph curve, when must a no-passing zone be marked, and what happens if the next no-passing zone begins less than 400 feet later?
model_answer: Direct Answer: On a roadway with center line markings, a no-passing zone must be marked at a curve where the passing sight distance is less than the Table 3B-1 minimum for the 85th-percentile speed or the speed limit (the specific 55-mph minimum sight distance value from Table 3B-1 is not included in the evidence provided). The zone must be marked with the one-direction or two-direction no-passing zone markings. If the next no-passing zone begins less than 400 feet away, the markings should be connected into a continuous no-passing zone. Standards (mandatory): - "On roadways with center line markings, no-passing zone markings shall be used at horizontal or vertical curves where the passing sight distance is less than the minimum shown in Table 3B-1 for the 85th-percentile speed or the speed limit." - "On two-way, two-lane or three-lane roadways where center line markings are installed, no-passing zones shall be established at vertical and horizontal curves and other locations where an engineering study indicates that passing must be prohibited because of inadequate sight distances or other special conditions." - "No-passing zones shall be marked by either the one-direction no-passing zone pavement markings or the two-direction no-passing zone pavement markings described in Section 3B.01 and shown in Figures 3B-1 and 3B-3." Guidance (recommended): - Where the distance between successive no-passing zones is less than 400 feet, no-passing zone markings should connect the zones. Citations: - Section 3B.03 Standard §4 (p.543) - Section 3B.03 Standard §3 (p.543) - Section 3B.03 Standard §1 (p.542) - Section 3B.03 Guidance §7 (p.543) - Section 2B.36 Support §3 (p.102)
gold_answer: The no-passing zone must be marked when available passing sight distance is less than 900 feet. If successive no-passing zones are separated by less than 400 feet, the markings should connect them.
